newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 54,000T corn, 72,000T wheat.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 54,000T corn, 72,000T wheat.

text.p: Taiwan traders said on Friday that they expect to see two tenders next week for a total of 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 72,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.
They said many Taiwan buyers believe that U.S. corn and soybean futures prices may drop further and that rising freight rates will keep buying interest slow in the coming week.
"Most of the buyers think corn and soybeans could drop further, so they are likely to stay sidelined until the futures prices drop or if the market shows bullish signals," one said.
Taiwan's FGEP corn buying group was expected to tender within two weeks for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn, traders said.

Despite the Taiwan Flour Mills Association's purchase of two 40,000-tonne wheat shipments on November 14, the group remains in the market for another two shipments of U.S. wheat totalling 72,000 tonnes, association official Lu Wei-chih said on Friday.
The two shipments would be slated for late December delivery, Lu told Reuters.
No exact date for the tender has been set, but Lu said the association would try to place it by November 29.
The domestic soymeal price for Taipei delivery was quoted at between T$9.7 to T$9.9 a kg -- the same same as a week earlier.
The corn powders price was at T$7.05 a kg for Taipei delivery, down from T$7.3 to 7.4 last week.
The local Pacific Northwest freight cost was about US$11 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico about US$21-22 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized February shipments.
The local flour price listed on Friday ranged between T$14.55 and T$15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.
